source.snippet: Every workout tracker I've tried has the same limitation: it records what you did, but it doesn't... [score: 28, 10 comments, tags: buildinpublic, ai, fitness, startup]

problem_statement: Existing workout tracking apps record exercise history but fail to provide actionable coaching intelligence — users want adaptive programming and insights, not just a log, and are paying for apps that don't deliver this.
target_segment: Fitness enthusiasts and intermediate-to-advanced gym-goers who already pay for workout tracking apps (e.g., Strong, Hevy, Fitbod) but want AI-driven adaptive programming
notes: Builder is actively building in this space (28 upvotes, 10 comments on dev.to indicates real audience interest). The framing 'logging is solved' implies the next problem is intelligence/coaching. Target users already pay $5–15/month for existing trackers, indicating willingness to pay. Competing products (Fitbod at ~$80/yr, Ladder, Future at $200/mo) confirm paid market exists. A solo operator could position as a smarter alternative to Fitbod.
